purpose: Fixed development sample for the ORS relational-table pipeline. Every routine CI run acquires, probes and parses only these chapters so a cycle stays cheap. Whole-edition runs are reserved for manual dispatch.
selectionPolicy: Chosen to span the structural cases the parser must survive, not to be representative of the statute book by volume. The roster is fixed: it changes only when a new structural case is identified, and the reason is recorded here.
notCorpus: This is a development sample, not a reviewed gold corpus and not the amendment parser's frozen 50-law certification corpus. Nothing here establishes correctness expectations.

chapters.rationale: First chapter in the book. Exercises the leading-zero file stem ors001.html and the low end of chapter sorting.
Residential landlord and tenant law. A long, heavily subdivided chapter with many centered subdivision headings.
General provisions of the criminal code. Dense with repeal and renumbering stubs, and with cited section ranges that produce the wrapped-citation lines the probe flags as ambiguous.
Construction of statutes. Small chapter, useful as a fast smoke case and as a lower bound on section count.
Public records and meetings. Sections carry long multi-session source credits, which exercises credit parsing.
Public contracting, general provisions. A lettered chapter, so it exercises the non-numeric chapter number path end to end.
Trade regulation. A lettered chapter high in the numbering, guarding against an assumption that letter suffixes only appear in the 200s.
